newsitem.title: INDIA: Mother Teresa to visit Europe, United States.
newsitem.headline: Mother Teresa to visit Europe, United States.

text.p: Mother Teresa, recovered from serious illness last year, plans to visit the United States and Europe on her first trip outside India after stepping down as head of her religious order, a spokeswoman of the Missionaries of Charity said.

The spokeswoman told Reuters on Sunday that the Nobel Peace Prize laureate was scheduled to leave on May 14 and was expected to return by the first week of August. Her trip will include a meeting with Pope John Paul.
"But this schedule may change depending on her health condition," the spokeswoman added.

Mother Teresa, plagued by illnesses which forced her to be taken to hospital three times last year for emergency care and heart surgery, stepped down as the head of the Missionaries of Charity earlier this year.
On March 13, Sister Nirmala succeeded her as the head of the religious order.
Dr Ashish Kumar, regular physician of the 86-year old Roman Catholic nun, said Mother Teresa's condition had improved since she was discharged from a heart clinic on December 19 last year.
"She is quite mobile now and fit to travel. She has shown amazing power of recovery," Kumar added.
Mother Teresa, known as Saint of the Gutters for her devotion to the poor and dying, would first go to Rome where she is expected to meet the Pope, the spokeswoman said.
"She is keen to meet the Pope, but no date has been finalised so far. It will all depend on the schedule of the two," she added.
Mother Teresa's last few visits outside India have been marred by ill health.

On her visit to Europe in 1993, she injured three ribs after a fall. In 1991, on her last trip to the United States, she fell ill midway through the trip and had to undergo first of her three heart operations.

"Mother is likely to be accompanied by a senior sister and Dr Patricia Aubanel, who came to Calcutta for mother's third heart surgery in November last year, during her trip to Europe and America," the spokeswoman said.
